purpose: Authoritative-provider delta adding Katana Cloud Inventory / Katana MRP as a manufacturing inventory, production and procurement source. Reuses REST/OpenAPI, static bearer credential, webhook and reconciliation fabric. No credentials, customer data, production mutation, payroll mutation, private-network access or paid services were used.

systems.name: Katana Cloud Inventory
systems.evidenceNote: Provider-owned Katana documentation confirms an OpenAPI 3.0-described HTTPS REST API at api.katanamrp.com, account API keys in the Authorization Bearer header, OAuth 2.0 for public app partners, page/limit pagination with X-Pagination metadata, common created_at/updated_at filters, soft-delete inclusion on supported resources, inventory/production/procurement resources, and HMAC-SHA256 signed webhooks. Endpoint documentation consistently exposes 429 throttling but no universal numeric quota is assumed. No authorised tenant was used, so effective account/key scope and read authority remain unproven.
securityEvidenceBlockers: Katana account API keys authenticate the same API surface that exposes production, inventory and commercial mutations. Before authentication evidence advances, prove account binding, key rotation/revocation and keep an executor-enforced exact GET/read route allowlist; successful Bearer authentication is not evidence of least privilege.

Katana documents that invalid filter parameters may be silently ignored. Generated incremental filters must be contract-validated before dispatch and response/reconciliation bounds must prevent a typo or schema change from silently widening a read to the full account.

Webhook registration is a mutating bootstrap action. Normal WFM runtime must not create/change webhooks without explicit authorised setup; use customer-controlled provisioning where possible and retain only the HMAC verification token plus constrained read credential for reconciliation.

Katana MCP can read and create/update operational records and is an agent/action surface. It is excluded from the normal WFM connector runtime and must not inherit integration credentials or mutation authority.

requiredPermissions: use a dedicated Katana API key for server-side integration only; never expose it client-side or place Authorization material in evidence/logs
pin HTTPS host api.katanamrp.com and reviewed v1 GET routes; disable arbitrary endpoints and cross-host redirects
keep POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE and MCP action surfaces disabled in steady-state WFM

if webhooks are used, separate registration authority from runtime, validate x-sha2-signature over the raw request body using the webhook token, bind event/account identity and deduplicate before processing
prove account/location scope, key replacement/deletion revocation, effective denied mutations and intended API-plan entitlement in an authorised tenant before tenant-authenticated evidence
dataAvailableOrExpected: manufacturing orders with stable IDs, order numbers, variant/location references, statuses including blocked/in-progress/done and created/updated timestamps
manufacturing-order production records and recipe/ingredient rows including material availability states such as in-stock, expected and not-available
product operations with product/variant/operation/resource identifiers and names, supporting work-centre/resource demand enrichment
operators and users, including shop-floor/warehouse working-area context and resource association where configured; operational identity only, not authoritative HCM/payroll
current inventory by variant/location, batch stock with batch/location/variant identifiers, and inventory movement history
inventory replenishment signals with account-wide 30-day average demand, stock risk, in-stock/committed/incoming context, safety-stock breach projection and lead-time evidence
products/variants, locations/warehouses, purchase orders/suppliers and sales/customer context where customer authorisation requires them
signed webhook events for supported object changes, treated as low-latency signals rather than completeness proof
stableIdentifiers: preserve Katana integer source IDs for manufacturing orders, productions, variants/products, operations/resources, operators/users, locations, batches, movements, purchase orders, suppliers and customers
namespace all external IDs by Katana customer account/connection; preserve location_id separately for multi-location operations
business order numbers and SKUs are matching aids, not substitutes for provider source IDs

freshnessLatency.rest: polling cadence is WFM-configured and bounded by provider 429 responses; updated_at filters support incremental reads on many list resources
freshnessLatency.inventorySignals: 30-day demand calculation is recalculated nightly at 07:00 UTC and may be up to 24 hours old; other signal fields can react faster to stock/supply changes
freshnessLatency.webhooks: low-latency best-effort signal; provider retries after failed delivery but REST backfill/reconciliation remains mandatory for completeness

paginationDeltaEvents.pagination: list endpoints use page/limit, default 50 and maximum 250, with X-Pagination metadata including total records/pages and last-page indicator
paginationDeltaEvents.delta: common list filters include created_at_min/max and updated_at_min/max in ISO 8601; use overlap windows, stable-ID dedupe and source timestamps because filters are not a universal transaction log
paginationDeltaEvents.deletes: include_deleted is available on supported resources and must be explicitly read where soft-deletion matters; absence from an incremental window never implies deletion
paginationDeltaEvents.webhooks: HMAC-SHA256 x-sha2-signature over the raw request body; deduplicate because delivery is not exactly once; reconcile REST after missed/outage periods

rateLimitsAndRetries: endpoint contracts expose HTTP 429 but no single universal numeric quota is hard-coded; adapt concurrency and use bounded exponential backoff with jitter for idempotent reads
401 stops blind retry and enters credential diagnostics; it never changes endpoint/version or broadens scope
invalid filter parameters can be ignored by the provider, so query/filter names and types must be validated against the pinned schema before sending
checkpoint only after complete pages; page gaps, partial failures or changed X-Pagination metadata trigger overlap replay/reconciliation rather than record deletion
webhook delivery may be duplicated or delayed; idempotency keys/source IDs and REST backfill protect recovery
versionsRegionsCustomFields: current public REST route is v1 and the API is provider-described with OpenAPI 3.0; pin reviewed schema/version rather than assuming future compatibility
Katana is cloud-based and supports multi-location operations; preserve account and location identity rather than collapsing sites
public documentation reviewed does not establish customer-selectable API data residency or regional API hosts; residency/cross-border claims require contractual or tenant evidence
preserve source timezone/UTC timestamps, locale, currency and UOM without implicit conversion; any customer-defined/custom fields remain schema-attributed extensions until mapped
MCP is a separate AI/action surface at mcp.katanamrp.com and is not an alternate connector transport for normal WFM ingestion
automationOpportunities: join manufacturing-order backlog, status and operation/resource demand to WFM availability/skills to forecast qualified cover, overtime or agency labour before capacity becomes urgent
use recipe ingredient availability plus inventory/replenishment risk to prevent paid labour being scheduled onto jobs that are materially blocked and redirect capacity to executable work
combine multi-location stock and production demand with worker availability/skills to support cross-site redeployment decisions without conflating location inventory
join production actuals/status changes to authoritative WFM pay cost for labour-per-order/good-unit analysis and outcome tracking
use purchase/supplier and stock-risk evidence to distinguish procurement-driven schedule risk from workforce-driven risk
bootstrap products, orders, operations/resources, locations, inventory and procurement from one SaaS source for smaller manufacturers, reducing implementation mapping effort
use signed webhooks for low-latency change signals while scheduled REST overlap/reconciliation repairs duplicates, out-of-order delivery and missed events
savingsHypotheses: reduce paid idle time by identifying material-blocked manufacturing work before scarce skilled labour is assigned
reduce overtime/agency spend by detecting production-capacity gaps from order/resource demand earlier in the planning window
reduce implementation effort for micro/SMB manufacturers because one cloud connection can populate production, inventory, location and procurement dimensions
improve stock/labour decisions by distinguishing account-wide sparse replenishment risk from full location inventory rather than treating every data feed as a complete snapshot
improve root-cause attribution by separating supplier/inventory constraints from workforce constraints when production misses occur
causalOutcomeReadiness: preserve account/connection, location, source object ID, schema fingerprint, source/effective timestamp, ingestion/recovery timestamp and dataset coverage kind on every mapped record
preserve recommendation/action identifiers and baseline/outcome windows when staffing changes are made against production/material signals

retain competing changes such as inventory receipt/transfer, order status/priority, recipe/material availability, supplier delivery, location change and production completion so throughput movement is not falsely attributed to labour changes
dataGaps: no authorised Katana tenant or API key was available to prove account binding, practical throttling, effective key authority, real schemas, location scope, archived/deleted behaviour or denied mutations
Katana user/operator objects are operational context and do not establish employment contracts, pay, absence, skills/certifications or authoritative attendance
public documentation reviewed does not prove customer-selected API data residency or regional endpoints
inventory_signals is intentionally sparse, account-wide and demand-window based; it cannot substitute for location-level full inventory
no universal exactly-once event or universal CDC contract exists; completeness requires REST reconciliation
constraintsRisks: API access requires an eligible Katana plan, so lower-tier/smaller customers may need the existing file/manual/iPaaS route rather than API automation
API credentials can potentially reach mutation routes; method/route allowlisting is mandatory regardless of key possession
invalid filter parameters can be silently ignored, creating a risk of accidental broad reads or false incremental completeness unless schema-validated before dispatch
webhooks are best-effort/duplicate-capable and their creation is a write action; runtime must separate bootstrap authority and reconcile via read API
MCP intentionally supports operational create/update actions and must remain outside WFM connector/agent authority
account-wide inventory signals can be misinterpreted in multi-site decisions unless coverage scope and location semantics are preserved
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Obtain an authorised Katana Professional-or-higher test tenant. Prove dedicated API-key account binding, replacement/deletion revocation, exact read-route authority and denied writes; execute paginated inventory/manufacturing-order reads with updated_at overlap, include_deleted/tombstone handling, invalid-filter fail-closed diagnostics, multi-location identity, timezone/currency/UOM/schema behavior, and signed-webhook duplicate/out-of-order/retry/backfill recovery. Keep MCP and all production/inventory/commercial mutations disabled.
